result: In 47 CFS vs 34 controls, plasma 8-iso-PGF2a isoprostanes were higher (P=0.007 and P=0.03 in high and low CV-risk subgroups), oxidised LDL higher (P=0.02) and HDL lower; in low-risk patients isoprostanes correlated with symptom score (P=0.005) and PEM (P=0.027).
reason: Independent cohort with a gold-standard lipid peroxidation marker raised, same direction as the oxidative-stress finding; not among cited studies.

result: GC-MS showed the urinary CFSUM1 and CFSUM2 'markers' were partly derivatised pyroglutamic acid and serine, artefacts of sample preparation, so earlier reported abnormalities were artefactual.
reason: Methodological debunking of a urinary assay; does not measure blood metabolome differences, so it neither tests nor contradicts the finding.

result: Salivary cortisol and cortisone were lower in medication-free CFS patients across the day (06:00-21:00) with lower rhythm-adjusted mean and amplitude, unshifted phase and unchanged cortisol/cortisone ratio.
reason: Independent cohort, salivary free cortisol lower, same direction; small sample.

result: Frequent 24-h blood sampling in 15 medication-free CFS vs 10 controls found reduced ACTH (especially 08:00-10:00, earlier acrophase) but no difference in cortisol level or cortisol circadian rhythm.
reason: Tests cortisol over 24 h and finds no difference; plasma total rather than free cortisol and very small, so weak contradiction.

result: In 32 adolescents with CFS vs 167 controls, joint mobility, Beighton score and collagen breakdown markers did not differ, while systolic BP was lower (adjusted -13.5 mmHg), skin extensibility higher (+0.3 SD) and arteries stiffer.
reason: Same measure (Beighton) in a paediatric population and finds no excess hypermobility, contrary to the finding.

result: PBMC microarray (3800 genes) before and after cycling at 70% predicted max showed exercise-responsive genes differed between women with CFS and controls, with ion transport and ion channel differences present at baseline and exaggerated after exercise.
reason: Same paradigm (post-exercise leukocyte mRNA) but different genes and untargeted microarray, so it extends rather than replicates the specific receptor-gene result.

result: In 23 adolescents with CFS vs 17 controls, a low-dose (500 ng/m2) synacthen test gave significantly lower mean cortisol levels, with more pronounced effects in females.
reason: Blunted cortisol response to ACTH, same measure and direction, in an adolescent population with a sex difference.

result: A meta-analysis of controlled CFS trials found a pooled placebo response of 19.6% (95% CI 15.4-23.7), lower than expected and lower than in other conditions, and lower for psychological interventions (meta-regression p=0.03).
reason: Measures the placebo response directly and finds it low, the opposite of the finding's claim that it is large.

result: In 12 CFS vs 11 controls, 09:00 plasma cortisol (367 vs 331 nmol/l), 24-h urinary free cortisol (182 vs 178 nmol/24 h), DHEAS and IGF-1 did not differ, nor did ACTH/cortisol responses to oCRH or naloxone.
reason: Tests 24-h urinary free cortisol, a measure named in the finding, and finds no difference; very small.

result: After the Trier social stress test, LPS-stimulated IL-6 and TNF-alpha production fell in 21 CFS patients but rose in 20 controls, with normal cortisol responses; patients did not show exaggerated LPS-induced cytokine secretion.
reason: Same measure (stimulated cytokine responses to a microbial antigen, after a challenge) but finds attenuated rather than exaggerated responses.
